studies.finding: Arterial connexin deletion reduces selected coupling readouts and restricts or delays propagated cortical vascular responses. Local and far-bin nulls, remaining small-vessel tracing and alternative carriers constrain a complete mechanism.
limitations: Adult mice of both sexes, overall age range 8-41 weeks. BMX:CreERT2 Gja4fl/fl Gja5fl/fl animals and Cre-negative double-floxed controls both receive tamoxifen. The driver targets arterial endothelium beyond the brain, including aorta; it is not a capillary-only or brain-only intervention. Assay-specific age/sex distributions are not fully resolved.

No prospective sample-size calculation. Genotype-blinded functional imaging acquisition and randomized stimulus order are reported; random stimulus order is not random genotype allocation. Pre-unblinding exclusions lack a complete animal manifest. The Gja4 floxed allele has an oocyte hypomorphism; same-flox controls do not establish equivalence to wild-type physiology.

Aortic electrophysiology uses six cells from only two mice per genotype; tracer loading uses six control and eight mutant fills from two mice per genotype. Cell-level tests do not supply six or eight independent animals. Apparent capacitance includes the coupled network, not just one cell surface. These are aortic recordings, not brain endothelial voltage recordings.

Retinal SERT tracing uses viral overexpression and terminal transcardial serotonin loading under anesthesia, 6-9 weeks after tamoxifen. Large-artery spreading events require favorable loading and occurred in only two of four controls; single-cell fills occurred in all four mutants. This selected qualitative tracing cannot determine a population conductance or physiological serotonin pathway.

Cx37, Cx40, Cx43 and Cx45 reporter distributions describe vascular segments; expression alone does not measure coupling strength or signal direction. Small-vessel tracer persistence is qualitative. A two-gene arterial deletion does not isolate the function of each isoform or test a selective isoform swap.

Focal visual two-photon imaging measures relative diameter; widefield IOS measures an optical HbT-related response. Neither IOS nor the derived response-propagation speed is a calibrated blood-flow, RBC-velocity, oxygen-use or electrical-conduction measurement. General functional analyses select arteries with baseline diameter greater than 15 micrometers.

Visual activity distance uses normalized, thresholded widefield GCaMP, which is biased toward upper cortical layers. The threshold does not prove absence of deeper or sparse activity. Optogenetic distance instead uses a postmortem ChRmine-expression mask, not simultaneous firing measurements. Histological arterial masks are manually registered and refined, not generated causal geometry.

Motion, pupil and locomotion corrections and signal-selection rules affect the analyzed response. In two-photon processing, selected low-power traces are set to zero by an analysis rule. Linear mixed models account for nesting in functional comparisons; the separate resting-diameter test treats vessels as independent despite nesting within mice.

Optogenetic stimulation uses two-second ChRmine pulse trains and six mice per genotype. The zero-laser condition can retain spontaneous vasomotion and imaging-light opsin activation; it is not an opsin-negative control. Functional imaging days 14-16 after viral injection do not specify a universal post-tamoxifen interval.

Propagation velocity is derived from the inverse slope of optical-response onset time versus position along a selected artery, with onset at ten percent of a sigmoid fit. Figure 5E calls it the slope, whereas Methods specify the inverse. Velocity analysis reports thirty averaged repeats, while the general optogenetic protocol reports ninety per power across sessions; subset selection requires clarification.

Full-screen noise differs from focal circles in spatial coverage and pattern. The comparison does not isolate energetic demand, and oxygen consumption or ATP supply is not measured. Time-to-peak genotype differences depend on distance bin; the farthest optogenetic and full-field bins are nonsignificant, not evidence of equivalence.

Resting microvascular control measures capillary RBC velocity near 100 micrometers depth, not whole-brain perfusion or RBC flux. Tail-cuff systolic/diastolic pressure is a separate systemic control. Nonsignificance in these small cohorts does not demonstrate physiological equivalence.

PMC author-manuscript passages and the author-hosted in-press PDF were read, including main Figures 1-6 and supplementary Figures S5-S7. Selected Methods cover the admitted assays; general cloning/culture methods and remaining supplemental material were not fully audited. Final bibliographic pagination is 5003-5019.e22, whereas the read in-press PDF ends its Methods at e12; version completeness remains unresolved.

Separate statistical/genotyping Tables S1-S2, allele-map files and movies were not obtained or replayed. Raw measurements are available from the authors on request and have not been obtained. The paper identifies code DOI 10.7910/DVN/XRRGRI, but public repository access failed; code files were not inspected or executed. No numerical edge weights or independent experimental reproduction are claimed.

Aortic electrical measurements, retinal tracer spread and awake cortical responses are distinct preparations. Cerebral endothelial voltage is not recorded along the full route. Gap junctions can carry small molecules as well as current; residual vascular responses and alternative routes prevent identification of a unique complete neural-to-vascular mechanism.

studies.finding: Partial astrocyte ablation reduced passivity; activation suppressed swimming. NE-MO activation increased astrocyte calcium and suppressed swimming in intact fish. Probabilistic feedback altered calcium accumulation.
limitations: Larval zebrafish, 5-7 days post fertilization; sex undetermined. The fictive-swimming assay uses paralyzed, restrained animals and tail motor-nerve signals, not displacement.

About half the fish did not show open-loop passivity and were excluded from subsequent analyses. Passivity is operationally an inter-swim interval of at least five seconds, not a report of hopelessness or human cognition.

Ablation is partial and may have indirect effects. gfap-driven tools may retain low neuronal expression; activation may affect other ions and second messengers. Convergent controls constrain but do not eliminate these caveats.

The glia-to-neuron molecular mechanism and unique evidence-accumulation algorithm remain unresolved. No universal glial class, minimal cell count, perfect intervention or independently reproduced experiment is asserted.

studies.finding: Peripheral challenges evoked neural readouts, while selected neural manipulations changed circulating cytokines. Activation improved high-dose endotoxin survival but increased bacterial tissue load in a different live-infection protocol. A complete descending immune circuit is not identified.
limitations: Both male and female mice at least seven weeks old were used; exact age and sex distributions per assay group are not supplied. No randomized animal allocation, blinded investigation or prospective statistical sample-size calculation is reported. The reporting summary discusses stimulus ordering separately; it does not establish randomized animal groups.

FOS labeling is an activity-associated marker; Vglut2-cre bulk GCaMP6s is a population calcium signal, not a DBH-specific spike recording. Photometry uses saline on day 4 and LPS on day 5 in the same animals. Vagotomized mice form a separate group after two weeks of recovery; a matched abdominal sham is not explicitly specified in the reviewed procedure. Figure 1c reports residual responses after an approximately 80% reduction.

LPS doses differ across assays: 50 micrograms/kg for FOS and TRAP, 0.5 mg/kg for the main photometry comparison, 0.1 mg/kg for cytokine chemogenetics and 12.5 mg/kg for survival. These exposures are not interchangeable. LPS endotoxaemia is distinct from viable bacterial infection.

Fos-based TRAP2 labeling is followed by at least four weeks before functional rechallenge to restore LPS sensitivity. LPS-TRAPed, Dbh-cre, Vglut2-cre and Vgat-cre populations are not identical. Dbh expression does not measure norepinephrine release or identify a unique molecular mediator.

For standard cytokine chemogenetics, Methods specify CNO at 2 mg/kg twelve hours and 1 mg/kg one hour before challenge; schematics and captions show only the one-hour pretreatment. mCherry controls receive CNO. Saline/LPS tests use the same cohort at least seven days apart, whereas hM3Dq/hM4Di versus mCherry comparisons use separate groups. Blood ELISA at two hours does not identify cytokine-producing cells.

Cre-defined nodose activation perturbs marker-defined neurons; it is not selective activation of the TRPA1 channel or CALCA peptide. TRPA1 neurons include different stimulus-responsive subgroups. Extended Data 8e shows two IL-10/fat co-responders among 63 neurons, which the authors did not consider further. Universal zero overlap is unsupported.

Injected cytokines and extraintestinal perfusion have different doses, routes and recording windows. The response classifier uses baseline median absolute deviation, a mean modified z-score above 1.6 and peak fluorescence of at least 1%. Selected, normalized responder heatmaps are not an unbiased full-population distribution. In vivo responses do not establish direct cytokine binding to a neuronal receptor; epithelial or immune intermediates remain possible. Referenced imaging procedures have not been fully audited.

Survival experiments use separate Trpa1-cre nodose and Dbh-cre cNST cohorts after high-dose LPS, with repeated 5 mg/kg CNO dosing. Figure 6 shows survival through nine days, not a lifelong or clinical outcome. Separate infection experiments use oral Salmonella and eight CNO injections beginning twelve hours before inoculation; bacterial load is measured in spleen and mesenteric lymph nodes at day five.

Nonsignificance is not equivalence or proof of no pathway contribution. The corticosterone null is a two-hour circulating concentration, not complete exclusion of hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal mediation. Extended Data 3 reuses the Figure 2c saline/LPS data; it is not an independent replication.

The cNST transcriptomic atlas pools tissue from five animals; 4,008 cells and expression clusters are not independent animal replicates, anatomical coordinates or a measured connectome. Rabies labeling supports an anatomical input interpretation, not synaptic efficacy. Main text calls the rabies reporter dsRed while Methods and Extended Data 12 specify GFP; panel 12d depicts Trpa1 but repeats Calca in its quantitative caption. No tracing fraction is calibrated.

Descending efferent routes and immune effector cells remain unresolved. A whole-animal Myd88 knockout does not isolate immune-cell-specific mediation. Lower circulating inflammatory cytokines do not imply universally better defense: sustained TRPA1-population activation increased Salmonella tissue burden in the separate live-infection assay.

Raw measurements, animal identifiers and custom code have not been obtained or replayed. Exclusion criteria include unsuccessful targeting/expression/ablation, but counts and operational thresholds are incomplete. Extended Data 9c reports Gpr65 IL-6 P=0.03 despite a broad no-appreciable-effect conclusion; its small plotted decrease must not be turned into an all-population null. No numerical edge weight or universal carrier count is assigned.

The DSS Methods specify CNO in the experimental cohort drinking solution, while Figure 6 says all animals received CNO. Matched control exposure and intake need resolution before a selective DSS mechanism is admitted. This issue does not change the separately described injected-CNO LPS or infection protocols.
